items.title: Mehrabad Airport, Tehran, Iran: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, attending Khamenei's funeral in Tehran, described him as a great scholar and leader, and said Pakistan and Iran will march together under all circumstances.
items.description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, attending Khamenei's funeral in Tehran, described him as a great scholar and leader, and said Pakistan and Iran will march together under all circumstances.
items.rawSummary: Funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at Mehrabad Airport drew over 9 million attendees and foreign delegations amid explicit calls for revenge against the U.S. and Israel, exposed regime divisions over Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's prolonged absence, and unfolded against a backdrop of suspended ceasefire talks with Washington.
items.analysis: The funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with over 9 million attendees, continued at Mehrabad Airport, drawing foreign delegations including Houthi representatives who chanted 'Death to America' and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who said Pakistan and Iran would march together under all circumstances, while red flags of revenge were waved and explicit calls to assassinate President Trump were prominently displayed, including from religious eulogist Mehdi Rasooli who declared at the farewell ceremony that Trump's assassination was 'our responsibility.' Senior military advisor Yahya Rahim Safavi later declared that an existential war is underway between Iran and Israel, vowing Iran would not be defeated, Israel would be wiped out, and Khamenei's blood would be avenged. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei remained absent reportedly due to assassination fears, and his prolonged absence has exposed regime divisions, with President Pezeshkian, according to The New York Times, warning of economic collapse and threatening to resign to push forward ceasefire talks with Washington, which President Trump told Axios were suspended for the funeral week. Iran announced it is collecting evidence for legal action over Khamenei's assassination and appointed Ali Ozmaei as the new IRGC Navy commander, while the military acknowledged using the ceasefire to upgrade combat capabilities; on the sidelines of the burial, Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami told Mojtaba Khamenei that those behind the killing 'must know that we will not let them off the hook.' Amid the ceremonies, a visit by IRGC General Vahidi reportedly turned chaotic, underscoring the volatile atmosphere, and American nationals also attended the funeral, with American Communist Party official Christopher Helali declaring 'I am here to defend Iran,' according to MEMRI.

items.description: Fars News reported the killing of multiple Iranian cyber scientists from the Handala hacking group, with unconfirmed assessments suggesting the entire unit may have been eliminated.
items.rawSummary: Iran's leadership transition proceeds with Mojtaba Khamenei consolidating power and the military vowing revenge, while the U.S. claims military success, Tehran pursues oil sales with Japan, and state-affiliated media reports a cyber unit has been killed.
items.analysis: The funeral procession for late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is underway, and Iranian Army Commander Major General Amir Khatami publicly pledged to avenge his blood, underscoring the military’s defiant posture. Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not appeared publicly since March, is consolidating authority by replacing the judiciary chief with a closer ally and reaffirming support for anti-U.S. resistance. U.S. President Donald Trump claimed the United States had ‘totally defeated’ Iran militarily and destroyed a newly installed radar, while Vice President JD Vance credited strikes for three days of free commercial transit in the Strait of Hormuz and asserted Iran is further from a nuclear bomb than in decades. Iran, however, has refused nuclear inspectors and only partially reopened the strait, and oil exports have surged; it began talks with Japanese companies to resume oil sales under a U.S. sanctions waiver, though buyers seek longer waiver periods and ship safety reassurances. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned of a possible third strike, a GCC official denied knowledge of a rumored $300 billion reconstruction package, and Fars News reported the killing of multiple cyber scientists from the Handala hacking group, with unconfirmed assessments suggesting the entire unit may have been eliminated.

items.title: South Korea, South Korea: Leveraged and inverse ETF assets tied to SK Hynix swelled to $19 billion, more than four times its average daily trading volume, while Samsung-linked leveraged ETFs reached $12.4 billion, nearly double its daily turnover; a single 2x leveraged long SK Hynix ETF held assets roughly twice the daily traded value of its shares.
items.description: Leveraged and inverse ETF assets tied to SK Hynix swelled to $19 billion, more than four times its average daily trading volume, while Samsung-linked leveraged ETFs reached $12.4 billion, nearly double its daily turnover; a single 2x leveraged long SK Hynix ETF held assets roughly twice the daily traded value of its shares.
items.rawSummary: South Korea's record export surge, driven by AI-related semiconductor demand, is accompanied by unprecedented leverage in stock markets, with single-stock ETFs tied to SK Hynix and Samsung reaching assets many times their underlying daily trading volumes.
items.analysis: South Korea's export sector posted a record performance in the second quarter of 2026, reaching approximately $270 billion, propelled by surging semiconductor and computer-related shipments tied to global artificial-intelligence investment. June exports jumped 59.5 percent year-on-year, accelerating from the already strong 53.4 percent gain in May. This economic momentum coincides with a dramatic buildup in leveraged exchange-traded fund assets, which hit a record ~$45 billion—an 800 percent surge since the start of the year—pushing leveraged exposure as a share of free-float market capitalization to an all-time high of ~2.9 percent. The concentration in single-stock products tied to chipmakers is particularly stark: leveraged and inverse ETFs tracking SK Hynix now hold about $19 billion in assets, more than four times the stock's average daily trading volume, while those tied to Samsung have roughly $12.4 billion, nearly double its daily turnover. A Hong Kong-listed 2x leveraged long SK Hynix ETF alone commands assets roughly twice the average daily traded value of SK Hynix shares, far exceeding comparable products for major U.S. technology stocks. The rapid accumulation of leveraged bets alongside booming exports highlights both the strength of the AI-driven economy and the potential for destabilizing deleveraging if sentiment shifts.

items.rawSummary: Indonesian special forces recover body of US pilot killed in Papua attack
items.analysis: Indonesian special forces recovered the remains of American pilot Nicholas F. Goselin following an attack by armed separatists on his aircraft shortly after it landed at a remote airstrip in Indonesia's Papua region. The pilot was killed in the assault. His body is now being transferred to the US Embassy in Jakarta for repatriation, with the State Department assisting the family. The incident underscores the persistent security threats in Papua, where separatist violence has claimed multiple victims in recent years.

items.title: Hong Kong, China: Data show Chinese semiconductor exports to Hong Kong hit a record $15 billion in May, with the territory absorbing over 50% of China's total chip exports in the first five months of 2026.
items.description: Data show Chinese semiconductor exports to Hong Kong hit a record $15 billion in May, with the territory absorbing over 50% of China's total chip exports in the first five months of 2026.
items.rawSummary: Chinese semiconductor exports through Hong Kong surge to record levels, with the territory now handling over half of China's total chip trade.
items.analysis: Chinese semiconductor exports to Hong Kong jumped to a record $15 billion in May, marking an increase of over 200% since early 2025. Over the first five months of 2026, China exported $239 billion of chips globally, with Hong Kong absorbing more than half of that total — a record proportion that has climbed steadily from roughly one‑third a decade ago. In May alone the territory accounted for 43% of China's semiconductor exports, while overall Chinese chip exports tripled over the same period. The trend points to Hong Kong's emergence as a dominant logistics and transshipment hub for China's semiconductor trade, a role that has significant implications for global supply chains and technology export controls.

items.title: Tokyo, Japan: Japanese retail investors purchased a record $5.9 billion net of domestic equities in the week ended June 26, while foreign funds sold $7.7 billion; AI-linked stocks saw sharp drops, but the Nikkei 225 surged 37% in Q2 2026, its best quarter on record.
items.description: Japanese retail investors purchased a record $5.9 billion net of domestic equities in the week ended June 26, while foreign funds sold $7.7 billion; AI-linked stocks saw sharp drops, but the Nikkei 225 surged 37% in Q2 2026, its best quarter on record.
items.rawSummary: Japan is in talks to resume Iranian crude oil purchases for the first time since 2019, while domestic retail investors have been buying Japanese equities at a record pace, offsetting heavy foreign outflows, amid a broader AI-driven stock rally.
items.analysis: The talks mark a potential shift in Japan’s energy imports, which have not included Iranian crude since 2019 amid sanctions. Resumption could signal changing diplomatic calculations and affect global oil trade flows. No agreement has yet been reached. Meanwhile, Japanese retail investors purchased a record net $5.9 billion in domestic equities during the week ended June 26, the largest weekly total on record, even as foreign funds sold $7.7 billion, the largest outflow since March. AI and semiconductor-linked stocks such as SoftBank, Kioxia, and Furukawa Electric each fell at least 12% last week, but the Nikkei 225 surged 37% in the second quarter of 2026, its best quarterly performance on record, driven by AI-related names.

items.title: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States: The National Mall was evacuated due to inclement weather ahead of President Trump's planned Independence Day speech.
items.description: The National Mall was evacuated due to inclement weather ahead of President Trump's planned Independence Day speech.
items.rawSummary: Fourth of July events in Washington were disrupted by heat and later storms that forced the evacuation of the National Mall, while President Trump discussed Iran negotiations, Israeli relations, and domestic political issues.
items.analysis: An Air Force major's uniformed protest at the Capitol remains under Pentagon investigation, while Defense Secretary Hegseth's troop-cut plans are paused for review. President Trump, who had earlier threatened Iranian asset seizures, now claims Iran is 'begging to make a deal' and both sides agreed to pause nuclear talks following Ayatollah Khamenei's death; Trump remarked he was surprised by the grief displayed by millions at the funeral, suggesting the tears might be fake, and said the U.S. could strike the assembled leadership but would refrain to preserve negotiations. A senior U.S. official told Axios that many of Trump's advisers believe Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu was wrong about everything, even as Trump said Netanyahu requested a White House meeting and could visit as soon as next week, adding that 'he knows who the boss is.' Domestically, Trump demanded the Senate end the filibuster and pardoned six individuals, while the Justice Department defied a federal court order to hand over redacted Epstein files; a severe heat wave canceled D.C.'s Independence Day parade, and hundreds of masked Patriot Front members marched through downtown areas near the National Mall, with a separate 'We The People 250' march moving toward the White House. Trump's 2025 disclosure showed over $2 billion in income, and June jobs data revealed a large gap between payroll and household surveys amid downward revisions. On the trade front, the U.S. goods deficit widened sharply in May to $105.8 billion, the largest since March 2025. In the evening, inclement weather prompted the evacuation of the National Mall ahead of a planned speech by President Trump, and the Great American State Fair and FIFA Fan Zone were postponed; a flyover involving the VC-25B presidential aircraft and four F-22 fighters was conducted despite the weather warnings.

items.rawSummary: Fourth of July events in Washington were disrupted by heat and later storms that forced the evacuation of the National Mall, while President Trump discussed Iran negotiations, Israeli relations, and domestic political issues.
items.analysis: An Air Force major's uniformed protest at the Capitol remains under Pentagon investigation, while Defense Secretary Hegseth's troop-cut plans are paused for review. President Trump, who had earlier threatened Iranian asset seizures, now claims Iran is 'begging to make a deal' and both sides agreed to pause nuclear talks following Ayatollah Khamenei's death; Trump remarked he was surprised by the grief displayed by millions at the funeral, suggesting the tears might be fake, and said the U.S. could strike the assembled leadership but would refrain to preserve negotiations. A senior U.S. official told Axios that many of Trump's advisers believe Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu was wrong about everything, even as Trump said Netanyahu requested a White House meeting and could visit as soon as next week, adding that 'he knows who the boss is.' Domestically, Trump demanded the Senate end the filibuster and pardoned six individuals, while the Justice Department defied a federal court order to hand over redacted Epstein files; a severe heat wave canceled D.C.'s Independence Day parade, and hundreds of masked Patriot Front members marched through downtown areas near the National Mall, with a separate 'We The People 250' march moving toward the White House. Trump's 2025 disclosure showed over $2 billion in income, and June jobs data revealed a large gap between payroll and household surveys amid downward revisions. On the trade front, the U.S. goods deficit widened sharply in May to $105.8 billion, the largest since March 2025. In the evening, inclement weather prompted the evacuation of the National Mall ahead of a planned speech by President Trump, and the Great American State Fair and FIFA Fan Zone were postponed; a flyover involving the VC-25B presidential aircraft and four F-22 fighters was conducted despite the weather warnings.

items.title: Mehrabad Airport, Tehran, Iran: Religious eulogist Mehdi Rasooli declared at Khamenei's farewell ceremony that 'Trump's assassination is our responsibility,' reinforcing calls for revenge against the United States.
items.description: Religious eulogist Mehdi Rasooli declared at Khamenei's farewell ceremony that 'Trump's assassination is our responsibility,' reinforcing calls for revenge against the United States.
items.rawSummary: Funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at Mehrabad Airport drew over 9 million attendees and foreign delegations amid explicit calls for revenge against the U.S. and Israel, exposed regime divisions over Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's prolonged absence, and unfolded against a backdrop of suspended ceasefire talks with Washington.
items.analysis: The funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with over 9 million attendees, continued at Mehrabad Airport, drawing foreign delegations including Houthi representatives who chanted 'Death to America' and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who said Pakistan and Iran would march together under all circumstances, while red flags of revenge were waved and explicit calls to assassinate President Trump were prominently displayed, including from religious eulogist Mehdi Rasooli who declared at the farewell ceremony that Trump's assassination was 'our responsibility.' Senior military advisor Yahya Rahim Safavi later declared that an existential war is underway between Iran and Israel, vowing Iran would not be defeated, Israel would be wiped out, and Khamenei's blood would be avenged. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei remained absent reportedly due to assassination fears, and his prolonged absence has exposed regime divisions, with President Pezeshkian, according to The New York Times, warning of economic collapse and threatening to resign to push forward ceasefire talks with Washington, which President Trump told Axios were suspended for the funeral week. Iran announced it is collecting evidence for legal action over Khamenei's assassination and appointed Ali Ozmaei as the new IRGC Navy commander, while the military acknowledged using the ceasefire to upgrade combat capabilities; on the sidelines of the burial, Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami told Mojtaba Khamenei that those behind the killing 'must know that we will not let them off the hook.' Amid the ceremonies, a visit by IRGC General Vahidi reportedly turned chaotic, underscoring the volatile atmosphere, and American nationals also attended the funeral, with American Communist Party official Christopher Helali declaring 'I am here to defend Iran,' according to MEMRI.
